doc: Rust's builtin types, and how the symbolic types are spelled in them.

notes.map: An ordered map, so that generated code serializes the same way twice.
notes.bytes: Base64 text on the wire, so this is a wrapper that reads and writes it, not a bare `Vec<u8>`, which serde writes as an array of numbers.
notes.any: Held as parsed JSON, since Rust has no dynamic type of its own.

types.name: u64
types.doc: An unsigned 64-bit integer. Travels as text, because half its range is outside i64 and JSON numbers cannot be trusted with the rest.

types.name: i128
types.doc: A 128-bit integer. Travels as text for the same reason.

types.name: f32
types.doc: A 32-bit float. Widening to f64 loses nothing; narrowing back does.

types.name: char
types.doc: A single Unicode scalar value, which travels as a one-character string.
